task: Best available images of the 21 letters as Dee recorded them, for redrawing the Enochian glyphs as filled ink outlines from the manuscript.
rules_kept: Every outline is to come from manuscript ink: Sloane MS 3188 f. 104 (primary) and Sloane MS 3189. The 1659 engravings are evidence for structure where the manuscript ink is knotted, not a source of outlines.
The owner's reference images (enoch-ink/refs/ref1-chart.webp, ref2-svg-pack.jpg, ref3-fontspace.jpg) were not opened, traced or used in this step.
Downloads are kept in their own folders (dl-commons, dl-wellcome, dl-archive, dl-bl, dl-whitby); scripts are in tools/; crops in crops/; scratch views in work/.
Names and values are reported as Dee's table gives them in Whitby's transcription; the hand of f. 104 and the meaning of the second form above Veh are left open.

summary.best_manuscript_image: Sloane MS 3188 f. 104: the Wikimedia Commons ORIGINAL, 4303 x 1603 px (SHA-1 verified), not the 1920 px rendering used so far. It is the best witness for the ink outline of all 21 letters: largest (letters 142-212 px tall), hard-edged, every form whole. Its weakness is that it is bitonal: where ink runs together it is solid black.
knots_and_blots_on_f104: Un - lower half knotted (crossing bar, turn of the stem and foot in one mass)
Or - lower half blotted (the bars at the foot run together)
Ged - eye of the inturned hook filled
Pal - dot joined to the stem by a hair-thin neck
summary.resolved_by: Sloane MS 3189 (Commons original, 1085 px, greyscale) shows each of these as separate strokes, small (letters about 46 px tall); Casaubon's Holy Table (1659) shows Un, Or and Ged clean but regularised (no Holy Table instance of Pal). Use 3189 for the course of the strokes and the engraving to confirm it; keep the weight and extent from f. 104.
summary.best_casaubon_images: Wellcome IIIF full-resolution PNGs (lossless output of the Wellcome image server; same capture as the archive.org copies, which are JPEG-recompressed). The archive.org original JP2 captures are the same pixels uncropped, marginally crisper. Copy 2's Holy Table is scanned about 1.2x larger than copy 1's (border letters about 105 px against 85 px) but hides the left border in the fold.
summary.british_library: Not reachable. The BL catalogue still lists Sloane MSS 3188 and 3189 as digitised but "(digital images currently unavailable)"; the viewer host access.bl.uk no longer resolves (DNS), api.bl.uk (the old IIIF manifests) is refused at the proxy (HTTP 502 on CONNECT), and no current BL manifest address could be found. No BL image was obtained.
summary.new_identity_evidence: Whitby's transcription of Sloane MS 3188 (Birmingham PhD thesis, 1982) gives Dee's own table of 26 March 1583 (f. 64b) with each name and Latin letter, in the order Pa b, Veh c, Ged g, Gal d, Or f, Un a, Graph e, Tal m, Gon i, Na h, Ur l, Mals p, Ger q, Drux n, Pal x, Med o, Don r, Ceph z, Van u, Fam s, Gisg t; and his commentary says the characters of 26 March are 'from right to left those transliterated at 64b, 2-22. The forms are more clearly defined in a later Action (see 104a, 30-31)', i.e. the f. 104 drawing. This is a scholarly source for the order the module calls unconfirmed.

images.character: Essentially bitonal: hard 1-px edges (about 0.36 mid-tone pixels per edge transition), no integer pixel replication, PNG 96 dpi. Looks thresholded from a photograph or microfilm, so filled counters and knots carry no tonal information. 2.24x the pixel size of the 1920 px rendering used so far; letters 142-212 px tall instead of 63-95.
images.folio_note: Commons: f. 104. Commons chart File:Enochian_alphabet.png: 'page 103v-104r'. Whitby's transcription (vol. 2, p. 391) puts the drawing at f. 104a, lines 30-31, the entry of 8 May beginning at f. 104b; his commentary (vol. 1, p. 449) cites it as '104a, 30-31'.

holy_table_copy1_cells.note: 84 border cells (positions 1-84, numbered as in plates/enochian/manifest.json: top 1-21 left to right, right 22-42 top to bottom, bottom 43-63 left to right, left 64-84 top to bottom) plus 4 corners, each turned upright (tops toward the table centre -> up); centre letters 85-96 row by row. Full resolution, no resampling except the exact 90/180 deg turns. Cell boxes come from straight lines fitted to the border rules (the page is not flat; residuals up to 15 px), so a few cells clip a neighbour.

holy_table_copy2_cells.note: Copy-1 cells mapped onto copy 2 by a homography fitted on SIFT matches (2449 inliers, median reprojection error 1.8 px), then cut and turned the same way. Positions 64-84 (left border) show only the facing leaf: the left border lies in the binding fold in this copy.

holy_table_mapping.note: Which of the 21 forms each Holy Table shorthand token is, judged by shape against the f. 104 forms (positions from the checked shorthand in plates/enochian/manifest.json, all re-cut here from the IIIF PNG). The plate prints no values; this is a form match, not a reading.

whitby.citation: Christopher Lionel Whitby, 'John Dee's actions with spirits: 22 December 1581 to 23 May 1583', 2 vols, PhD thesis, University of Birmingham (repository date 1982; the title pages say 'Submitted ... October 1981').
whitby.rights_as_stated: PDF p. 2: 'This unpublished thesis/dissertation is copyright of the author and/or third parties ... Further distribution or reproduction in any format is prohibited without the permission of the copyright holder.' Used here for reading only; its hand-drawn letter forms are a modern copy and are not to be traced or reproduced.
read: Vol. 2, p. 235 [64a]: the angel shows characters 'enclosed in no lines: but standing by them selues, and points betwene them', Dee notes them in the line (l. 45), and the angel counts them 'being 21: and begynning from the right hand, toward the left' (margin: '21 Characters').

Vol. 2, pp. 236-237 [64b]: each name as the angel spoke it, with Dee's marginal column of form, name and Latin letter (Pa b ... Gisg t, as listed in summary.new_identity_evidence); Dee notes sounds, e.g. 'Ceph, sownded like Keph', 'Pal the p being sownded remissly'.

Vol. 2, p. 238 [64b]: the 21 forms written right to left in three groups of seven over their Latin letters 't s u z r o x | n q p l h i m | e a f d g c b', and, below, one further form with 'y' under it; Dee's marginal note (marked with his delta) 'Thus I deciphered them after a day or two or three'.
Vol. 1, p. 449, note to [64a] l. 45: 'These letters are from right to left those transliterated at 64b, 2-22. The forms are more clearly defined in a later Action (see 104a, 30-31).'

Vol. 1, p. 145: 'The Enochian alphabet consists of twenty-one characters, the addition of a dot to a previous character making an alphabet corresponding to twenty-two letters as in Hebrew (see fol. 64b).'

Vol. 2, pp. 390-391 [104a]: 'Maij 6 ... the perfect forms of the holy letters receyuing ... When E K could not aptly imitate the form of the Characters, or letters, as they were shewed: that then they appered drawn on his paper with a light yelow cullor, which he drew the blak vppon ... after this manner, and iust of this quantitie and proportion.' followed by the two lines of letters (lines 30-31), with the small form above the second from the right; p. 391 marks f. 104b as beginning with the entry for 8 May.
open_points: Whitby's hand copy of the extra form over 'y' (vol. 2, p. 238) looks like his copy of the t-form (Gisg) with a dot, not like Gon. The module (following an enthusiasts' site) says the dotted letter is Gon. This rests on a modern hand copy and must be checked on the manuscript (f. 64b), which could not be reached.

Whitby's copies of the 26 March forms differ from the 6 May forms for some letters (e.g. Veh is drawn K-like, Tal 7-like, Van x-like). The K-like C in the heading of Casaubon's Specimen may reflect that earlier form; not checked on the manuscript.
f. 64b in the manuscript itself (Dee's ink of the first table) would be a third ink witness for every letter; no image of it was obtained.

casaubon_specimen.note: Heading of 'A Specimen of the Tables or Book of ENOCH' (both copies agree glyph for glyph). Reading right to left against 'Pagesgem' and 'Bacap', the forms for P (Mals), g (Ged), m (Tal, with three dots) and B (Pa) are the f. 104 forms, as the module says. Two further observations, unresolved: the A of 'Pagesgem' is the Holy Table's Or-form (oblique stem, hooked top, bars at the foot) with two dots, not Un; the C of 'Bacap' is K-like, as Whitby draws Dee's first form of Veh.

method: Letter boxes on both Commons originals found as connected ink components and cut with padding (24 px f. 104, 6 px 3189) at native resolution.
Per-letter measurements (work/stats-f104.json, work/stats-3189.json): height, connected components and enclosed counters at a fixed threshold, edge width.

Knots and blots judged by eye on the full-resolution crops and on 4x (f. 104) and 8x (3189) enlargements, side by side with the Holy Table cells of both copies (crops/compare-view/, a viewing aid only: panels are rescaled).
note_on_paths: Paths are those of the working folder the images were downloaded to; the images and crops themselves are not kept in the repository. Every image is identified by its source URL and checksum.
